I'm a 33-year-old Muslim living with my parents. They charge me $200 a month, which is market rate where we live, so that's fair. Recently, there was a toilet flood in my bathroom, so they had to remodel my section, which means we're running into each other a lot more than before. I used to lock myself in my room most of the time, but now that's not possible. Today, my parents went to Costco. When they got home, I was sitting on the couch playing Apex Legends. My mom asked me to help bring in the groceries, and I told her I'd do it in a minute. I was too into the game to notice that they made several trips back and forth. Finally, my dad told me to get my ass up, and I again said I'd do it in a minute. He said that "in a minute" was now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. That led to a huge shouting match, and now they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday, which is basically impossible. They also brought up my younger brother, who is married with two kids and just got promoted at his job. They're using him as the golden child, throwing his success in my face, which I find bullshit. I mean, I could have gotten up and helped them, but because I pay rent, I feel like I have the right to say no when they ask for help with things like groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole here? Alright, so breaking this down. First, I'm living with my parents, paying rent, which is fair. They're not taking advantage of me financially. However, I'm an adult, and I'm supposed to be independent. But I'm still living with them, which might be seen as not fully independent. However, I'm paying my way, so that's a point in my favor. When my parents asked me to help with groceries, I was playing a game and told them I'd do it in a minute. They ended up making several trips, and my dad got frustrated, leading to an argument. I think the issue here is communication and respect. My parents probably felt that I wasn't contributing to the household despite living there, and when they asked for help, I was dismissive. I also mentioned that I avoid them most of the time, which might make them feel neglected or unappreciated. The remodel situation forced more interaction, which might have been a trigger for the argument. My dad took the controller, which escalated things, but I was also uncooperative. Another point is the comparison to my younger brother. They're using his success against me, which is hurtful and unfair. It's a common tactic in family arguments, but it's not constructive. So, am I the asshole? I think I have some responsibility here. While I pay rent, living with parents often comes with certain expectations, even if they're not explicitly stated. Helping out with household tasks is part of being a contributing member. My dismissive attitude and refusal to help when asked could be seen as selfish, especially since I'm an adult and should be capable of handling such responsibilities. On the other hand, my parents might have overreacted by checking into a hotel and expecting me to find a place by Friday, which is unrealistic. They could have communicated their feelings more calmly and discussed the situation instead of escalating it. In conclusion, while I have some valid points about paying rent and wanting to play a game, my refusal to help and the way I handled the situation contributed to the conflict.
